about: The read rule behind the stored daily wellness series: which reading a day shows when several sources recorded the same metric that day. Watch before phone before third-party. Changing anything below changes what the rule computes and needs a new ruleVersion in the same edit.

tierRule.device: A device is tiered by its manufacturer and hardware model when it states both: a manufacturer matching no tier's pattern is third-party. Only a device stating neither falls back to its name and model.
tierRule.reading: A reading naming a device the pod describes takes that device's tier. A reading naming none takes its source's tier.
tierRule.source: A source's tier is the tier its device-bearing records predominantly name; a tie goes to the better tier. A source with no device-bearing record is third-party, whatever it is called.
tierRule.sameSource: Records of one reading type, statistic and day from one source and device are one source's versions of that day: the one from the most recent import wins, dated by the newest export (its own ExportDate) listing the pack that lists the record's sample group. A record no dated export reaches ranks below every dated one. Version 1 kept the one with more samples, which keeps an aggregate from before a sample was deleted.

alternatives: Other sources (source and device) that reported the same reading type and statistic that day. A source's older versions of the day are not alternatives.
